changes.before: After push_back, read at(2) instead of at(0). Which value is selected?
changes.after: Store a growing list of values in a vector.

before: std::vector<int> stores a sequence of integers and manages its own storage. <vector> declares the type; the angle brackets select its element type.
push_back adds an element at the end. size() gives the number of currently stored elements, not an index.
at(0) reads the first element. at checks bounds and reports an out-of-range access by throwing; exception handling is taught later. operator[] does not provide that same check.
For three values, valid positions are 0, 1, and 2. Do not deliberately execute an invalid unchecked access.
Expected output or behavior: 2 3. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Append a new score and predict its index and the new size. Use checked access rather than testing invalid unchecked positions. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: A vector stores a sequence of values and manages the space they need. std::vector<int> stores integers. Include <vector> to use it; the angle brackets name the type of each item.
push_back adds one item at the end of the vector. size() reports how many items the vector currently holds.

at reads an item at a chosen position. It checks whether that position exists. If it does not, at throws an exception: an error that interrupts the normal path. A later lesson explains how to handle one.
An index is an item's numbered position. Indexes start at zero. A vector with three items has indexes zero, one, and two.
The program prints 2 3. scores.at(0) reads the first value, two. scores.size() returns three because push_back added a third item.
size() is the number of items, not the last valid index. Square-bracket access does not provide at's bounds check. Use a position that exists before reading an item.

Predict the changed case before choosing.
Explain why, then optionally try the local transfer.
Return to the preceding idea and compare what changed.

before.question: After push_back, read at(2) instead of at(0). Which value is selected?
choices: 3 because size is the final element.
6 because index 2 is the third stored value.
before.explanation: Zero-based positions identify the third appended value at index 2.

after.question: After push_back, change at(0) to at(2). Which value does it read?
choices: 3, because the size is the last value.
6, because index 2 selects the third value.
after.explanation: The vector holds 2, 4, and 6. Their indexes are 0, 1, and 2.
